We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list. Need number of methyl groups (CH3). Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, also maybe 20-30. In data we have peaks at 58.70 (likely O-CH3 or CH2 attached to hetero), 36.40 (two identical), 26.40. Also aromatic carbons around 124-168. So methyl likely 26.40 maybe. Also 58.70 could be methoxy (O-CH3). That's also a methyl. So total methyl groups maybe 2? Need to confirm if 36.40 are methylene (CH2) not methyl. Methylene carbons around 20-40. 36.40 could be CH2. So methyl groups: 58.70 (O-CH3) and 26.40 (alkyl CH3). So answer 2.

But could there be more methyls not observed? Use proton NMR to confirm. Let's get proton NMR.
